title_en: Clearing After Rain on Mount Inwang
key_facts: Painted by Jeong Seon in 1751, late in his life.|Depicts Mount Inwang in Seoul as mist clears after rain.|A key work of 'true-view landscape' (jingyeong sansu): painting real Korean places rather than idealized Chinese scenes.|Dark, wet ink masses on the rock faces contrast with the pale mist.|Entered the National Museum of Korea through the Lee Kun-hee donation (2021).

title_en: Album of Genre Paintings by Danwon (Ssireum wrestling, Village School, etc.)
medium: Ink and light color on paper
key_facts: An album of scenes of everyday life in late Joseon by Kim Hong-do.|Famous leaves include 'Ssireum' (Korean wrestling) and 'Village School'.|Figures are drawn with quick, lively brush lines and little or no background.|In 'Ssireum', spectators sit in a circle around two wrestlers.|Shows ordinary people working and playing, not only the elite.
source_note: 작성자 기억에 의한 초안. 화첩 구성 점수·전시 중인 장면 확인 필요

key_facts: Kang Se-hwang painted himself at about age 70 (1782).|He wears an official's black gauze hat together with informal scholar's robes, an unusual combination.|His own inscription explains the combination: his mind is in the mountains and forests while his name is on the court roster.|Kang was a scholar-painter and art critic, and a teacher of Kim Hong-do.
